name: jyotish-engine
description: Open-source, client-side Vedic (Jyotish) chart engine and life-blueprint report generator. Computes entirely in-browser; no birth data ever leaves the user's device.

notes.ephemeris: @swisseph/browser chosen after empirical evaluation (see DECISIONS.md) -- computeRawPositions() in src/engine/ephemeris.ts is not yet wired to it. astro-sweph and swisseph-wasm were evaluated and rejected.
notes.geocoding: GeoNames cities15000 dataset is not yet bundled. See data/README.md for the download step (requires network access this environment doesn't have — do this step in Claude Code, not in a sandboxed chat session).
notes.main/types: Added 2026-08-07 so web/ (the free-tools SvelteKit app) can consume this package via a `file:..` dependency -- `npm run build` already worked (tsc -p tsconfig.json -> dist/, gitignored) but nothing pointed at its output until now. web/'s own package.json runs this build automatically (predev/prebuild) so dist/ can't go stale relative to src/; there is no watch-mode wiring yet, so an engine change requires web/'s dev server to restart (or a manual `npm run build` here) to pick it up.
notes.exports: Added 2026-08-07 alongside src/free-tools.ts, a second barrel (sibling to index.ts's computeChart() pipeline) for the free-tools cluster's own API surface (Panchang, dasha timeline, kundli/South Indian chart rendering, confidence checker, geocoding). Two subpaths only -- "." (index.ts) and "./free-tools" (free-tools.ts) -- deliberately not a per-module exports map, so a new tool needing something not yet exposed adds one line to free-tools.ts, not a new package.json entry. See DECISIONS.md.
